# Game compatibility

<!-- Generated from patches/<Game>/game.ini by scripts/gen-compatibility.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

This list shows what has been tried so far, on one setup (a Steam Deck with a PS Move ZCM1 and a PS3 Eye). It is a snapshot, not a promise: arcade games differ a lot, and some depend on the TeknoParrot runtime or on your own dump.
RavenGun ships no games. You need your own legally obtained copies.

## Working (7)

These games run on RavenGun's own loader and start straight from RavenGun (double-click), without TeknoParrot; they were played with the lightgun (PS Move or mouse) and checked on the TV. The note says what was tested.

- **HALO Fireteam Raven**: WORKING on our own route (2026-10-14): a double-click in RavenGun starts the game without scripts and without TeknoParrotUi (daemon -> rg-direct -> Wine -> BudgieLoader, input through the tp-shm I/O bridge). Measured on the TV in mouse mode: skip calibration with TEST twice (hold key 0 briefly), coin (key 5), START (key 1), aim, shoot, reload (right button), a kill; ran 5:12 min. The native route (Linux, own loader) also exists and skips calibration with START.
- **Jurassic Park Arcade**: WORKING: runs on our own loader, started straight from RavenGun (double-click; the RavenGun engine starts it itself, no scripts), native Linux, OpenGL on Vulkan (zink); played with a PS Move and with a mouse (2026-10-14). The lightgun board answers as the real USB board (RIO bridge, rio-invoer.ini): no more "RIO Disconnected"; START (key 1), aim and trigger work (score and kills measured), the game's own settings (free play, difficulty, volume, ...) are in the app. Four glow shaders Mesa rejected are fixed (data/shaders). Not measured: player 2's trigger, a physical mouse and the PS Move. See bewijs-speelbaar-20261014/LEESMIJ.md.
- **NERF Arcade**: WORKING: runs on our own core (native Linux, Nerf.x86_64), started straight from RavenGun (double-click; the RavenGun engine starts it itself, no scripts). The lightgun board (RIO) answers through the RIO bridge: START (key 1 / Move START), aim and trigger (mouse 2026-10-14: score 12,050). The Windows route (TeknoParrot, DXVK, BepInEx) is no longer needed. Not tested: player 2.
- **Rabbids Hollywood Arcade**: WORKING on our own route (2026-10-14): a double-click in RavenGun starts the game without scripts and without TeknoParrot (daemon -> Proton with our BepInEx plugin, input over TCP). Measured on the TV in mouse mode: coin (key 5), START (hold key 1 briefly), aim and trigger; ran 5:19 min with a played round. The dongle check (SBK.Matrix) is answered, see DONGLE-ONDERZOEK.md. Not yet measured: whether the savegame survives two starts, and playing with the real Move buttons.
- **Raccoon Rampage**: WORKING on our own route (2026-10-14): a double-click in RavenGun starts the game without scripts and without TeknoParrotUi (daemon -> rg-direct -> Wine -> OpenParrot loader). Measured on the TV in mouse mode: trigger = start, aim and shoot, played up to a boss (score 22046), ran 5:17 min. Coin (key 5), test menu (key 0, F3, F4); calibration is stored in the game's save data. Not yet played with the real Move on this route.
- **Terminator Salvation**: WORKING on our own route (2026-10-14): a double-click in RavenGun starts the game without scripts and without TeknoParrotUi (daemon -> rg-direct -> Wine -> BudgieLoader, full screen through gamescope). Measured on the TV in mouse mode: START (hold key 1 briefly), mission select with the trigger, aim, shoot, reload (right button), a kill; ran 6:32 min. Not yet played with the real Move on this route.
- **Tomb Raider Arcade**: WORKING on our own route (2026-10-14): a double-click in RavenGun starts the game without scripts and without TeknoParrot (daemon -> Proton with our BepInEx plugin, input over TCP). Measured on the TV in mouse mode: coin (key 5), START (hold key 1 briefly; a very short tap does not count), aim, trigger, a level played; ran 5:24 min. Not yet played with the real Move buttons.

## Playable (12)

These games start from RavenGun and can be played with the lightgun. Some are not yet confirmed with a real PS Move in every detail; the note says what was tested.

- **Gashaaaan Refill!!!!**: Playable after a one-time setup in the test menu (clock, screen, free play; now stored in the game's save data). Then start, aiming and trigger (the ball) work. Test menu: key 0, select with start, execute with P1 aux1.
- **Gashaaaan!!!!**: Playable: coin (key 5), start (key 1), aiming and trigger (the ball) work. First start shows 'BACKUP DATA ERROR': press TEST (key 0) once to repair. Free play can be set in the test menu (P1 aux1 = execute).
- **Go Go Strike**: Works: bowling with the Move as trackball (direction and swing set the throw), start (key 1) and trigger (click). 4:3 picture with black bars (gamescope).
- **House of the Dead: Scarlet Dawn**: Playable through the TeknoParrot UI (two programs: AM Daemon and the game): start (key 1), crosshair (measured at the corners and centre), trigger (left button) and sub trigger (right button, switches weapon) work; free play, one round played. Loading to the first stage takes about 1.5 minutes. Real Move buttons, player 2 and the test menu not tested.
- **Let's Go Island 3D: Lost on the Island of Tropics**: Playable: starts through to the attract, 3D calibration (red-cyan picture), start (key 1) and play. The crosshair follows the aim (measured on a grid in the cutscene) and the trigger fires. Loading takes about a minute. Real Move buttons and sound not checked.
- **Let's Go Island: Lost on the Island of Tropics**: Playable: starts through to the attract, start (key 1) and play. The crosshair follows the aim (measured on a grid) and the trigger fires. Fullscreen, no title bar. Loading takes about a minute. Real Move buttons and sound not checked.
- **Let's Go Safari**: Playable: the game starts through to the attract and driving (course choice and start with the buttons). Red, blue, yellow and green are the keys A, S, D and F, the wheel is the left and right arrow keys, coin is key 5. The steering keys change the picture (how much steering is not measured); the wheel from the Move's horizontal aim is not there yet; the window is not fullscreen.
- **Luigi's Mansion Arcade**: PLAYABLE ON OUR OWN CORE (2026-10-13, seen on the TV): ~6 min of continuous attract/demo, fullscreen via gamescope, no error banner; the owner watched. Solved with the per-game drop-in dropin/rg-pe-hook.dll (generic PE inline hook) which arms itself when the packer seals .text (NtProtectVirtualMemory -> 0x20) and then: (1) catches the game's OWN ExitProcess in its virtualized WinMain (return address VACUUM.exe+0xf1374d) and RETURNS instead of terminating; (2) writes the data-path string at RVA 0x3d0c20 (was empty -> crash on the first shader); (3) stubs the 17 am keychip functions, with amDongleIsAvailableInternal RETURNING 1 (not 0), else the game shows ERROR 0949 "Keychip Not Found" (measured). CORRECTION to the old reading: "exit code 32" is the low byte of a pointer, not a Capcom anti-tamper/COM block; patch 0005 is detection only. Input (tp-shm, Layout LuigisMansion) not yet played with the real Move.
- **Pigs Might Fly**: Playable: start (key 1) and trigger (the lever that launches the pig) work; portrait picture in the middle of the TV. Test menu: TEST (key 0), service (F3). Runs in its own Wine prefix where C:\Sega points at the game.
- **Rampage**: Playable, but not a lightgun game: a joystick-and-attack game for three players. Player 1: up = trigger, down = reload, left = grenade, right = aux1, attack = key F4, coin = key F5, start = key 1 (player 2: coin key 5, start key 2). Measured: intro movie, tutorial, climbing, walking left and right, demolishing buildings ($ 7,500). Runs with DXVK and gst-libav (AAC decoder for the movies); no crosshair. Real Move buttons, players 2 and 3 and the test menu not tested.
- **Time Crisis 5**: Playable through the I/O bridge (shared memory): aiming, trigger and left pedal (middle button) work; coin = the Move button for key 5 (the engine sends Shift+T to the game). Shoot '1-player solo' in the menu. The right pedal has not been checked on its own yet.
- **Transformers: Shadows Rising**: Playable with the Move: the engine acts as the gun board of the game (hid-board route). Crosshair checked on the TV (2026-10-11): within 1.5% of the screen at every grid point. Start (Move Start), trigger and aiming work; loading takes about 4 minutes.

- **Operation G.H.O.S.T.**: Started, not played. The game starts and keeps running (STARTTEST.md with our own loader; ZONDER-LADER.md with no loader at all, 20 and 70 s). The region/PCB dongle is not enforced: without any region source it starts anyway. Playability was not measured.
- **Rambo**: Never started: only a static study of the protection (BESCHERMING-STATUS.md). Rambo (Sega Lindbergh, 32-bit ELF): amDongle inside the ELF, the check is already forced in all four ELFs.

- **The House of the Dead 4**: Never started: only a static study of the protection (BESCHERMING-STATUS.md). The House of the Dead 4 (Sega Lindbergh, 32-bit ELF): amDongle Ver.0.05 inside the ELF, check path unpatched.
- **The House of the Dead 4 Special**: Never started: only a static study of the protection (BESCHERMING-STATUS.md). The House of the Dead 4 Special (Sega Lindbergh, 32-bit ELF): same amDongle layer as HOTD4, unpatched check path.
- **The House of the Dead EX**: Never started: only a static study of the protection (BESCHERMING-STATUS.md). The House of the Dead EX (Sega Lindbergh, 32-bit ELF): amDongle Ver.0.12, check already forced to succeed.
- **TNXK0O~C (unidentified Sega title)**: Never started: only a static study of the protection (BESCHERMING-STATUS.md). TNXK0O~C: unidentified Sega title (keychip Ver.1.12, SDDV_Table.dat, RingWide); the game's name is inferred, not established.

## Not working yet (17)

These games do not start, or are blocked by something RavenGun does not work around (for example copy protection). They are listed so you know what to expect; they may start working in a later version.

- **Gaia Attack 4**: Does not start yet: no picture. The Wine crash (MXCSR=0 caused by the loader) is worked around (RG_LOADER_FPFIX); the game runs through the JVS chain but stays black (no 0x20 polling). Parked; see games-status.md, eleventh round.
- **Galaga Assault**: Parked: TeknoParrot's loader does not get it past start-up under Wine. Measured statically (see patches/ELF-LADER-SPEC.md): 357 PLT stubs, of which 99 imports have a name and 258 have an erased name, together exactly 357; zero section headers and every stub pushes 0xdeadbeef, so lazy binding is impossible. The table that maps slots to names is not in the file. For Jurassic Park -- the same packer and the same class -- it was measured that the rt-glfix bridge removes the GL blocker but that the game then falls over on an unresolved non-GL import; for Galaga Assault that has not been measured yet. Waiting on the resolution table from a running ElfLdr2 run.
- **Ghostbusters**: The ElfLdr2 path check is solved. The loader requires all files of this game to be in a folder named pm (the Play Mechanix install root) with the path to the elf inside it; with [Identify] Path = pm/game and a view folder views/GhostBusters/pm with links to the game files it continues to "Starting Game". The game does not reach a picture yet; what blocks it then (dongle, OpenGL context) has not been measured. The pm folder is not a drop-in: its content is the owner's own dump (2.7 GB), see README.md.
- **Haunted Museum**: Does not start yet: no picture. The Wine crash (MXCSR=0 caused by the loader) is worked around (RG_LOADER_FPFIX); the game runs through the JVS chain but stays black (no 0x20 polling). Parked; see games-status.md, eleventh round.
- **Haunted Museum II**: Does not start yet: no picture. The Wine crash (MXCSR=0 caused by the loader) is worked around (RG_LOADER_FPFIX); the game runs through the JVS chain but stays black (no 0x20 polling). Parked; see games-status.md, eleventh round.
- **Infinity Blade FX**: Does not start yet: UE3 starts (needs Wine Mono and a first-run dialog for TeknoParrot.dll), then a white or black picture; the log stops at 'Kaboom: InitLib() failed'. Parked.
- **Lethal Enforcers 3**: Does not start yet: the game crashes when it opens a .m1v movie; Wine has no 32-bit GStreamer (lib32-gstreamer plus an MPEG-1 decoder), which the SteamOS repos do not offer. Parked.
- **Medaru No Gunman**: Does not start cleanly yet: picture, coin (key 5), reload, trigger and aim work, but on every fresh start the game reports 3001 RAM DATA IS BAD or 3003 ROM HAS CHANGED. After one pass through its test menu it plays (that process only). Window 1024x768, top left.
- **Men in Black**: Under investigation since 2026-10-14; see ATTRACT-RUN.md.
- **Metal Gear Arcade**: Assessed only (2026-10-14), not started. Konami AVS/e-Amusement; the only loader is TeknoParrot's closed TeknoMacaw -- no own-core route. See README.md.
- **Music GunGun 2**: Does not start yet: the Wine crash is worked around (RG_LOADER_FPFIX), but the game shows its own 'Direct3D initialisation failed' window (also with DXVK) and does not open the JVS pipe. Parked.
- **Omatsuri Yasan - Ganso Takoyaki**: Does not start yet: white window (1024x768), the game never creates a D3D device; the core makes an online activation request at start. Parked.
- **Omatsuri Yasan - Kingyo Sukui**: Falls over on our core with exit code 8, but not at the file layer: in the WINEDEBUG=+file trace the game process opens no file of its own, while the closed core does see it stay alive (still there after 20 s, measured with the same method). The previously mentioned missing campaign*.bmp is therefore not the cause of what we measure; the game never gets that far. What separates the two siblings: Takoyaki, which lives, has a GMDATA folder this game lacks, and their executables differ in size (643,072 against 1,642,496 bytes). The redirection folder our core creates (TeknoParrot/D through W) is empty, while rqrdlist.rqr does exist, in the game's own Media folder (1,200,082 bytes). A drop-in cannot land here: this game runs straight from the NAS and has no view.
- **Otomedius Excellent**: Inconsistent, and that is measured. With full logging (WINEDEBUG=+file,err+all) the game process only appears around 20 s and stays alive after that; in a fast run it leaves around 2 to 5 s with exit code 0. The marker that makes the difference is whether libacio.dll and libbms.dll get loaded: they are in the log of the closed-core run, and absent in the fast run. That fits the note that this game needs a BMS service next to ACIO on COM2 (the BMS pipe and bms_GGG.exe), so the cause is probably not an exit code but a missing second process. The profile also has the General/DisableFileCheckSum switch: 22 of the 191 data paks on the NAS differ (edited or translated), which gives a Conflict Hash and a clean exit. That switch is deliberately NOT enabled -- that is the owner's decision. Playability was not measured.
- **Pac-Man Chomp-Mania**: Parked: TeknoParrot's loader does not get it past start-up under Wine. Measured statically (see patches/ELF-LADER-SPEC.md): 442 PLT stubs, zero section headers, every stub pushes 0xdeadbeef and the GOT is already filled in the file with absolute 0xb7xxxxxx addresses from a running process on the original cabinet. The number of stubs equals the number of UND imports, but how many of those lost their name cannot be measured for this game: the UND table grows with whichever upper bound you pick, so the end of the table was not found here. Same class as Jurassic Park, where it was measured that the rt-glfix bridge removes the GL blocker but the game then falls over on an unresolved non-GL import. Waiting on the resolution table from a running ElfLdr2 run.
- **Rainbow Bombergirl**: Does not get past the start of the game: it starts through to the attract (two screens: portrait main screen on the right, touch screen bottom left), and the test menu (TEST key 0, service F3) and input check show every button, but after coin (key 5) and start it stays at SYSTEM ENTRY / the PASELI notice. Parked.
- **SilentHill**: Plays its attract movie on OUR OWN core (2026-10-13, on the TV) -- but is NOT playable: the replacement I/O library delivers no inputs yet (no buttons, coins or guns). What got it there: our own shaiolib.dll in the drop-in (the original waits for two serial boards and the security plug: "LOW CONTROL ERROR 5-1500"), a 32-bit GStreamer for Wine (without it the game quits when the opening movie should start), and a three-byte in-memory patch that removes the StopWhenReady call (without it the movie stays black). The region is Asia for now (model code GNGHLAAA); Europe needs a speaker setting the dump does not have. See ATTRACT-RUN.md.
